categories.title: Pages and flows
categories.summary: The screens people hit when a route is missing, data is empty, or the app is still working.

categories.title: Search engine optimization
categories.summary: Each public page tells a search engine what it is, in the page itself.

categories.title: Generative engine optimization
categories.summary: Assistants can tell who this is, what it does, and which facts are safe to quote.

categories.title: Answer and chat engine optimization
categories.summary: A person, or a chat engine, can answer the page's question without hunting.

categories.title: Legal and consent
categories.summary: Privacy, terms, payments, user content, and public claims are written down before someone has to ask.

categories.title: Identity and appearance
categories.summary: The app looks intentional on a phone, a desktop, and a browser tab.

categories.title: Looks designed
categories.summary: The screen looks like this product. Color, spacing, icons, and copy are chosen. Adapted from unslop by Damir Sokolovsky, CC BY 4.0.

categories.title: Interface details
categories.summary: Loading, keyboard, touch, and type behave the way a finished product does.

categories.title: Accessibility
categories.summary: People can reach, read, and operate the interface without a perfect setup.

categories.title: Performance
categories.summary: Images, fonts, and the first download do not punish the visit.

categories.title: Security
categories.summary: Secrets stay private, visitor input cannot take over the page, and private screens stay private.

categories.title: Forms
categories.summary: A form says what it wants, what went wrong, and when it succeeded.

categories.title: Accounts and settings
categories.summary: If people have an account, they can manage it and recover access.

categories.title: Project hygiene
categories.summary: Someone else can run the app, and the packages and data it depends on are looked after.

items.title: Custom 404 page
items.why: A missing route should still feel like the product and offer a way onward.
items.howToVerify: Open a URL that does not exist. Pass only if the app renders its own 404 with a way home. A framework default such as the plain Next.js, Vite, or host 404 does not pass.
items.howToFix: Add your own 404 page in the router or pages folder, with a link back home. A framework default page does not count.

items.title: Friendly error state
items.why: A crash or a failed request should explain what happened instead of a blank screen or a stack trace.
items.howToVerify: Find the production error UI, error boundary, or failed-request state. Pass if a person sees a designed message and a next step. Development overlays and raw stack traces do not pass.
items.howToFix: Add an error page or error boundary that says what happened and what to do next.

items.title: Loading states
items.why: Waits should look intentional, so people do not click twice or assume the app froze.
items.howToVerify: Find views that wait on a network or computation. Pass if they show a skeleton, spinner, or progress text. A skeleton shaped like the loaded layout is the stronger pass. A blank region or a control with no feedback does not pass.
items.howToFix: Wherever the screen waits on data, show a skeleton, a spinner, or the words Loading.

items.title: Empty states
items.why: A list, search, or dashboard with nothing in it still needs a sentence and a next step.
items.howToVerify: Find a collection, search result, or inbox that can be empty. Pass if that state explains itself. If the app has no collection that can be empty, mark not applicable and say why.
items.howToFix: When a list or search is empty, show a sentence and the next action, such as a button to create the first item.

items.title: Thank-you or confirmation page
items.why: After a signup, checkout, or important form, people need a clear end to the flow.
items.howToVerify: Submit the primary form, checkout, or signup. Pass if it lands on a confirmation screen or thank-you page. Mark not applicable only when the app has no form, checkout, or signup.
items.howToFix: After the main form, checkout, or signup succeeds, send the person to a page that says it worked.

items.title: Payment receipt or confirmation
items.why: A charge needs a receipt the person can recognize, with the amount and what they bought.
items.howToVerify: Trace the success path after payment. Pass if a confirmation shows what was purchased and that payment succeeded. Mark not applicable when the app never takes payment.
items.howToFix: After payment, show a confirmation with the amount and what they bought.

items.title: The price is shown before the charge
items.why: A person who never saw the amount, what it buys, or that a free trial becomes a paid plan can dispute the charge.
items.howToVerify: Find the step where they confirm payment. Pass if it shows the amount, what it is for, and when money will be taken, before they pay. If there is a free trial, that step says when the trial ends and what they will be charged then. Mark not applicable when the app does not take payment.
items.howToFix: Before payment, show the amount, what it buys, and the date of the charge. If a trial converts to paid, say so on that same step.

items.title: Unique meta title per page
items.why: Tabs, search results, and shares all use the title. One reused title makes every page look unfinished.
items.howToVerify: Compare document titles across public routes. Pass only if each public page has its own specific title. Titles that are only Home, a file name, or a framework default such as Vite + React do not pass.
items.howToFix: Give every public page its own title. Replace leftover titles such as Vite + React.

items.title: Unique meta description per page
items.why: The description is the sentence search engines and previews show under the title.
items.howToVerify: Check the meta description on each public page. Pass if each one is unique and describes that page. A missing, empty, or site-wide identical description does not pass.
items.howToFix: Add a meta description on each public page that describes that page only.

items.title: Canonical URL
items.why: A canonical link tells search engines which URL is the one to keep when the same page has aliases.
items.howToVerify: Look for a rel=canonical link on public pages, pointed at the preferred absolute URL. Pass if it is present and matches the real public URL.
items.howToFix: Add a canonical link on public pages that points at the preferred https URL.

items.title: Open Graph and Twitter cards
items.why: Shared links should show the right title, description, and image instead of a random scrape.
items.howToVerify: Look for og:title, og:description, og:type, and a Twitter card title. Pass if the public pages set them. An og:image is part of a full pass when the page is meant to be shared.
items.howToFix: Add og:title, og:description, and a Twitter card title on pages people will share.

items.title: Sitemap
items.why: A sitemap lists the public URLs you actually want discovered.
items.howToVerify: Find sitemap.xml, or the generator that publishes it, and confirm it lists real public routes. A sitemap full of drafts, admin URLs, or only the homepage is not a pass.
items.howToFix: Publish a sitemap.xml of the real public URLs. Leave admin and draft URLs out.

items.title: robots.txt
items.why: Crawlers need an explicit allow or disallow, plus a pointer to the sitemap when one exists.
items.howToVerify: Open robots.txt. Pass if it is intentional for this app and references the sitemap when a sitemap exists. A file that accidentally disallows the whole site does not pass.
items.howToFix: Add a robots.txt that allows the public site and points at the sitemap.

items.title: One clear h1 per page
items.why: The h1 is the page's title for people and for parsers. Competing h1s blur what the page is.
items.howToVerify: Inspect each public page's headings. Pass if there is one descriptive h1 and the lower headings nest in order.
items.howToFix: Keep one descriptive h1 on each page. Change extra h1s to h2s.

items.title: Descriptive alt text
items.why: Images that carry meaning need a text equivalent. Decorative images need an empty alt.
items.howToVerify: Review img elements and image components. Pass if meaningful images have specific alt text and decorative ones use alt="". Filenames, "image", or missing alt attributes do not pass. If the app has no images, say so and mark not applicable.
items.howToFix: Describe meaningful images in the alt text. Use an empty alt for decorative images.

items.title: Viewport meta tag
items.why: Without a viewport tag, phones scale the desktop layout and the app feels broken.
items.howToVerify: Find the viewport meta in the document head or the shared layout. Pass if width=device-width is set.
items.howToFix: Add the viewport meta tag with width=device-width in the shared head.

items.title: Dates on articles
items.why: A published or updated date tells readers and citation systems whether a post is current.
items.howToVerify: Open an article. Pass if a visible published or updated date is in the page. Mark not applicable when the app does not publish articles or posts.
items.howToFix: Show a published or updated date on each article.

items.title: llms.txt
items.why: A short llms.txt file gives assistants a map of what the site is and which pages to trust.
items.howToVerify: Look for llms.txt at the site root, or the file that deploys there. Pass if it names the product and points to the canonical pages. A file that only exists in a draft, and is not served, does not pass.
items.howToFix: Add llms.txt at the site root with the product name and links to the main pages.

items.title: Who, what, and who it is for
items.why: Generative engines quote a clear entity. A homepage that never says who operates it is easy to misidentify.
items.howToVerify: Read the homepage or about page. Pass if a person can state the name, what the product does, and who it is for without guessing.
items.howToFix: On the homepage or about page, say the name, what it does, and who it is for.

items.title: Quotable facts
items.why: Specific facts are what assistants can cite. Vague slogans get paraphrased into something you did not say.
items.howToVerify: Read the main marketing or about copy. Pass if concrete facts (what it does, who it serves, where it applies) are written in sentences a citation could lift. Slogans alone do not pass.
items.howToFix: Add a few concrete sentences about what the product does and who it serves.

items.title: Organization or author attribution
items.why: Named authorship or a named organization is how engines attach claims to a real entity.
items.howToVerify: Find a visible author, organization, or footer credit on public pages. Pass if the responsible party is named. An anonymous template with no operator does not pass.
items.howToFix: Name the person or company responsible in the footer or on the about page.

items.title: Structured data for the main entity
items.why: JSON-LD lets search and answer engines read the product, organization, or articles as data.
items.howToVerify: Look for JSON-LD that matches a real entity on the site, such as Organization, WebSite, Product, or Article. Pass if it agrees with the visible page. Placeholder schema with fake ratings does not pass.
items.howToFix: Add JSON-LD for the real organization or product, and make it match the visible page.

items.title: The first screen answers what this is
items.why: Chat engines lift the opening of a page. If the answer is below a long animation, they miss it.
items.howToVerify: Read each important public page from the top. Pass if the first screen states what the page is offering in plain language.
items.howToFix: Put a plain sentence at the top of each important page that says what that page is.

items.title: FAQ or question-style headings
items.why: Questions with direct answers are the unit chat engines prefer to quote.
items.howToVerify: Look for an FAQ or headings phrased as real questions, each followed by a direct answer. Pass if at least the main objections or common questions are answered that way. Skip marketing headings that only sound like questions.
items.howToFix: Add a short FAQ, with a direct answer under each question.

items.title: Consistent name and facts
items.why: If the name, price, or promise changes from page to page, both people and chat engines will mix them up.
items.howToVerify: Compare the product name, offer, and key facts across the homepage, metadata, and footer. Pass if they agree. Leftover template names do not pass.
items.howToFix: Use one product name and one offer in the page, the title, and the footer.

items.title: Privacy policy
items.why: People should be able to read what the app collects, why, and who receives it.
items.howToVerify: Open the privacy policy from a public footer or equivalent. Pass if it describes this app's actual data practices. A lorem ipsum policy, a policy for a different product, or a link that 404s does not pass.
items.howToFix: Publish a privacy policy for this app that says what you collect, why, and who receives it. Link it in the footer.

items.title: Terms of service
items.why: Terms set the rules of use before someone creates an account, pays, or relies on the app.
items.howToVerify: Open the terms from a public footer or equivalent. Pass if they belong to this product and are reachable. Placeholder terms do not pass.
items.howToFix: Publish terms for this product and link them in the footer. Remove placeholder terms.

items.title: Cookie banner and a refusal path
items.why: Non-essential cookies and analytics need a choice, including the choice to refuse them.
items.howToVerify: Load the app as a new visitor. Pass if a banner explains non-essential cookies and lets someone refuse them before they are set. Mark not applicable when the app sets no non-essential cookies and uses no analytics. A banner with only Accept does not pass.
items.howToFix: Ask before you set analytics or other non-essential cookies, and include a way to refuse.

items.title: Session replay is off or inputs are masked
items.why: A recording tool that catches passwords, cards, or messages stores more than a page view.
items.howToVerify: Search for a session replay tool such as Hotjar, FullStory, LogRocket, Clarity, or PostHog session recording. Pass if none is installed, or it stays off until the visitor opts in and password, payment, and message fields are masked. Mark not applicable when the app uses no analytics and no replay tool.
items.howToFix: Leave session replay off unless someone opts in, and mask password, payment, and message fields.

items.title: A way to reach a person
items.why: Privacy questions and support need a real contact path, not only a social icon.
items.howToVerify: Find a contact page, email, or support form from the public site. Pass if a person could use it to reach the operator.
items.howToFix: Add a contact page, email, or form that reaches the person who runs the app.

items.title: Favicon set
items.why: Tabs, bookmarks, and home-screen icons should show this product, not the framework logo.
items.howToVerify: Check the head for an icon, an apple touch icon, and a web manifest. Pass if those files exist and are not the default framework icon.
items.howToFix: Add your own icon, an apple touch icon, and a web manifest. Remove the default framework icon.

items.title: Theme color
items.why: The browser chrome should pick up the product color instead of a default gray or white strip.
items.howToVerify: Find a theme-color meta tag, and a matching color in the web manifest if a manifest exists. Pass if it is set on purpose.
items.howToFix: Add a theme-color meta tag in your brand color.

items.title: Responsive layout
items.why: A phone and a desktop should both be able to read and use the app without horizontal chaos.
items.howToVerify: Review the layout at a narrow width and a wide width, or inspect the CSS that does that work. Pass if primary tasks fit and text is readable. A desktop page that only shrinks via the browser zoom does not pass.
items.howToFix: Make the main tasks fit a phone width so the page does not scroll sideways.

items.title: Readable contrast
items.why: Low-contrast gray on a tinted background looks designed and then fails in daylight.
items.howToVerify: Check body text, labels, and buttons against their backgrounds. Pass if ordinary text is clearly readable, roughly a 4.5:1 contrast for normal text. Placeholder gray-on-gray does not pass.
items.howToFix: Darken light gray text until ordinary text is easy to read on its background.

items.title: Visible keyboard focus
items.why: If focus is removed, keyboard users cannot see where they are.
items.howToVerify: Look for :focus-visible or an equivalent that stays visible. Pass if focus is obvious. A global outline: none with no replacement does not pass.
items.howToFix: Keep a visible focus outline. If outlines were removed, put a clear replacement back.

items.title: Reduced motion
items.why: People who ask the system for less motion should not get large looping animations.
items.howToVerify: Search for prefers-reduced-motion, or confirm the app has no non-essential motion. Pass if motion is toned down or absent. Essential state changes can remain.
items.howToFix: Turn off non-essential animation when the system asks for reduced motion.

items.title: Skeletons match the loaded layout
items.why: A spinner on a blank screen jumps when the real layout arrives. A skeleton that flashes on a fast load feels broken too.
items.howToVerify: Find views that wait on data. Pass if they show gray blocks in the shape of the real layout, from the same structure as the loaded state, and those blocks stay hidden until the wait is longer than about 300ms. Pass if the app never waits after first paint. A skeleton that changes size when the content lands does not pass.
items.howToFix: Build the skeleton from the same component as the loaded state. Show it only after about 300ms.

items.title: Small actions update before the request returns
items.why: A like, a checkbox, or a rename that waits on the network feels stuck when the request almost always works.
items.howToVerify: Find likes, toggles, and renames that save in the background. Pass if the screen updates immediately and rolls back with an error when the request fails. A payment, or anything that moves money, waits for the server. Mark not applicable when the app has no small action like that.
items.howToFix: Update the screen first for likes, toggles, and renames, and put the old value back if the request fails. Leave payments until the server answers.

items.title: A keyboard command menu
items.why: People who use an app every day should not have to remember which menu holds an action.
items.howToVerify: Pass if Command+K on Mac and Ctrl+K elsewhere opens a search of the real pages and actions, and a result can be chosen from the keyboard alone. Mark not applicable when people do not use this product every day.
items.howToFix: Add a command menu of the real pages and actions. Open it with Command+K on Mac and Ctrl+K elsewhere, and make every result work without a pointer.

items.title: Shortcuts are visible where the action is
items.why: A shortcut nobody can see never gets learned.
items.howToVerify: Pass if menus, tooltips, or the command menu show each shortcut, using the Mac command symbol on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere. Shortcuts do not fire while focus is in a text field. Mark not applicable when the app has no keyboard shortcuts.
items.howToFix: Show each shortcut beside its action. Ignore shortcuts while the person is typing in a field.

items.title: Reversible actions offer undo
items.why: A confirm dialog gets accepted without reading. Undo is the confirmation people actually use.
items.howToVerify: Find delete, archive, and other reversible actions. Pass if the action happens immediately and an Undo notice stays for about 5 to 10 seconds, with role=status. The permanent change waits until that notice closes. A confirm dialog as the only gate does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no reversible destructive action.
items.howToFix: Do the action right away, show an Undo notice with role=status for 5 to 10 seconds, and delay the permanent change until the notice closes.

items.title: Cached screens show, then refresh
items.why: Going back to a screen you just left should not show a spinner.
items.howToVerify: Pass if cached data paints immediately and a refresh runs in the background, including when the window regains focus or the network returns. Balances, stock counts, and anything where an old number costs money stay fresh. Mark not applicable when the app has no data worth caching.
items.howToFix: Show the last result immediately, refetch in the background, and refetch again on focus and when the network returns. Do not cache balances or stock counts.

items.title: Same-site links are ready before the click
items.why: The next page can be ready while the pointer is still on the link.
items.howToVerify: Pass if same-site links are prefetched by the router or prerendered, and logout plus any link that changes data are left out. Speculation rules with moderate eagerness pass. Pass if the app has no same-site navigation. Mark not applicable for a native app.
items.howToFix: Prefetch same-site links with the router, or with speculation rules set to moderate eagerness. Leave out logout and links that change data.

items.title: Uploaded images show a blur first
items.why: A photo that pops in from an empty box shifts the page and shows the wrong colors first.
items.howToVerify: Pass if each uploaded image stores a tiny blur placeholder and shows it at the image's exact size until the file loads. Mark not applicable when nobody uploads an image. Reserving the box is a separate check.
items.howToFix: Store a BlurHash or ThumbHash with each uploaded image and show that blur in the image box while the file loads.

items.title: View changes move instead of swapping
items.why: A sudden swap between two views is harder to follow than a short move.
items.howToVerify: Pass if a same-page update can animate with a view transition, route changes can animate, and an element that moves between them shares one view-transition-name. The motion stays under 300ms. A browser without support may switch instantly. Pass if the app has no view change worth animating. Reduced motion is a separate check.
items.howToFix: Use a view transition for same-page updates and for navigation. Give a shared element the same view-transition-name on both screens, and keep the motion under 300ms.

items.title: Sheets follow the finger
items.why: A sheet that only closes from a button feels stuck when the person is already dragging it.
items.howToVerify: Find bottom sheets. Pass if the sheet follows the finger and closes on distance or a quick flick, and a close button remains. Mark not applicable when the app has no bottom sheet.
items.howToFix: Make the sheet follow the drag and close on a flick. Keep a visible close button.

items.title: Motion can be interrupted
items.why: An animation that has to finish before it listens makes the interface feel late.
items.howToVerify: Pass if motion the person can interrupt turns around from its current position and speed, and input is never blocked while something animates. A CSS keyframe on a control the person can grab does not pass. Pass if nothing on screen can be interrupted. Reduced motion is a separate check.
items.howToFix: Use a spring that can reverse mid-way. Remove keyframe animations from anything the person can interrupt, and do not block input during motion.

items.title: Back can preview the previous screen
items.why: A back swipe that shows the previous screen lets the person change their mind before they leave.
items.howToVerify: Pass if back handling can preview the previous screen, including the platform default when the app does not override the back button. An override that swallows the back gesture does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app does not target Android or React Native.
items.howToFix: Use the platform's predictive back callback. Leave the system default in place when you do not need custom back behavior.

items.title: Tap targets are larger than the icon
items.why: A small icon is hard to hit when the touch area is only as big as the pixels you see.
items.howToVerify: Pass if every control is at least 44 by 44 points on iOS and the web, and 48 by 48 dp on Android, even when the icon is smaller. Padding or a hit slop may make up the size. Overlapping targets do not pass.
items.howToFix: Pad each control, or set a hit slop, so the touch area meets that minimum without covering the control beside it.

items.title: Fixed bars clear the notch and the home indicator
items.why: A header under a notch, or a tab bar under the home indicator, cannot be tapped.
items.howToVerify: Pass if a full-bleed layout sets viewport-fit=cover and pads fixed edges with safe-area insets, or the native app pads for the safe area. A fixed bar that can sit under the notch, the Dynamic Island, or the home indicator does not pass. Pass if the app has no full-bleed fixed bar.
items.howToFix: Set viewport-fit=cover and pad the header and the bottom bar with the safe-area inset. In React Native, use the safe area insets.

items.title: A texted code fills in with one tap
items.why: A login code from a text should land in the field without retyping.
items.howToVerify: Find the code field. Pass if it is one input with autocomplete=one-time-code and inputmode=numeric, and the message ends with a line the platform can read, such as @yourdomain.com #123456. On iOS, a one-time-code content type passes. Mark not applicable when the app never asks for a code from a text or an email.
items.howToFix: Use one input with autocomplete=one-time-code and inputmode=numeric. End the message with @yourdomain.com and the code.

items.title: Changing numbers stay the same width
items.why: A price or a timer shifts sideways when a 1 is narrower than an 8.
items.howToVerify: Pass if timers, prices, counters, and numeric columns use tabular-nums. Pass if the screen has none of those.
items.howToFix: Set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on timers, prices, counters, and numeric columns.

items.title: Headlines do not leave one word alone
items.why: A heading with one word on the last line looks unfinished.
items.howToVerify: Pass if headings and short titles use text-wrap: balance, and paragraphs use text-wrap: pretty.
items.howToFix: Set text-wrap: balance on headings and text-wrap: pretty on paragraphs.

items.title: Large corners are smooth
items.why: A large radius drawn as a quarter circle looks tighter than a smooth corner on a big panel.
items.howToVerify: Pass if a large rounded panel sets corner-shape: squircle next to its border-radius. Pass if the interface does not use large rounded corners. Browsers that ignore corner-shape keep the radius.
items.howToFix: Add corner-shape: squircle beside the border-radius on large rounded panels.

items.title: Hover menus stay open on the way to a submenu
items.why: A submenu that switches while the pointer moves toward it makes the menu feel broken.
items.howToVerify: Find hover menus that open a submenu. Pass if the open panel stays open while the pointer moves diagonally toward it. Mark not applicable when the app has no hover submenu.
items.howToFix: Use a safe polygon, or the menu library's own version, so the submenu stays open while the pointer travels toward it.

items.title: Surfaces stay neutral
items.why: A hue-to-hue gradient, a glow, and gradient text on every card is the default look of a generated screen, so the product never gets a color of its own.
items.howToVerify: Review backgrounds, cards, buttons, headings, and charts on the main screen. Pass if surfaces come from one neutral ramp, text is a solid color, and a single accent appears only where it means something, such as the primary action, the selected row, or one key figure. A real brand color used as that flat accent passes, including purple when the brand is actually purple. A violet-to-blue or other hue-to-hue gradient, gradient text, a colored glow or glowing shadow, a radial color blob, a neon border, or a chart that paints every series in the accent does not pass. If the workspace has no visual screen, mark not applicable and say what it is instead.
items.howToFix: Remove decorative gradients, glows, and gradient text. Keep one neutral surface and one solid accent on the primary action or the one figure that matters.

items.title: Icons come from one set
items.why: Emoji in the navigation, on badges, and beside labels read as decoration a model added.
items.howToVerify: Review navigation, buttons, badges, empty states, and status labels. Pass if the screen uses one line-icon set at one size and one stroke, or uses no icons. An emoji used as an icon does not pass, including a sparkle on a New, Beta, or AI badge, or an emoji inside a count. Emoji inside a message a person wrote can stay. If the workspace has no interface, mark not applicable and say what it is instead.
items.howToFix: Remove emoji from labels, navigation, and badges. Use one line-icon set at one size, in the same color as the nearby text, or leave the icon out.

items.title: Spacing is on one scale
items.why: A 13px gap beside a 7px gap makes sibling rows and cards look accidental.
items.howToVerify: Compare padding, gaps, and row heights in the main layout. Pass if spacing sits on a 4px scale, sibling cards share one padding, and rows in one list share one height and one gap. Space inside a group is smaller than the space between groups. A 2px nudge inside a small control can pass. One-off values such as 7px, 11px, or 13px, or a list whose rows differ in height for no reason, do not pass. If the workspace has no laid-out screen, mark not applicable and say what it is instead.
items.howToFix: Move margins, padding, and gaps onto a 4px scale. Give sibling cards the same padding, and give the rows in one list the same height and gap.

items.title: Interface copy is plain
items.why: A greeting with an exclamation mark, or a headline like Supercharge your workflow, could sit on any generated page.
items.howToVerify: Read the headings, buttons, labels, and stat captions on the main screen. Pass if the headline says what this product does, labels are sentence case, and a change names its comparison, such as +12% vs last month. An exclamation mark, a Welcome back headline, a hype word such as supercharge, seamless, unlock, magic, or revolutionize, a label in widely tracked capitals, a heading at a weight of 800 or 900, or a trailing period on a button does not pass. A statistic or testimonial is judged on the reviews check. If the screen has almost no interface copy, mark not applicable and say so.
items.howToFix: Rewrite the headline so it says what this product does for the people it is for. Remove exclamation marks and hype words, set labels in sentence case, and say what a percentage compares to.

items.title: The first screen shows this product
items.why: A glossy blob, a glowing brain, or a centered stack of buttons does not show what the product does.
items.howToVerify: Look at the hero or the main app view. Pass if a landing page shows the product, or one concrete image of what it does, with one primary action and at most one secondary action. Pass if an app or dashboard is that product, with the accent used on one thing that matters. A glossy blob, orb, stock robot, glowing brain, circuit hologram, gradient logo tile with a sparkle, or a hero that is only a centered headline and several buttons does not pass. A headline that would still fit after swapping in another product name does not pass. A short working screen with no marketing hero can pass. If there is no visual interface, mark not applicable and say what it is instead.
items.howToFix: Remove filler art. Show the product, or one object from what it does, and keep one primary action with at most one secondary action beside it.

items.title: Motion explains a change
items.why: A pulsing glow, a card that grows on hover, and blocks flying in from every side are motion with nothing to say.
items.howToVerify: Search the styles for pulse, ping, bounce, hover scale, and load-in animation. Pass if motion is a short color or surface change, a small press, a menu that fades in, or the screen has no decorative motion. A looping pulse or ping on something that is not live, a card that scales up on hover, a bouncy spring, parallax, or a load animation that sends each block in from a different direction does not pass. Honoring reduced motion is a separate check. If the workspace has no interface, mark not applicable and say what it is instead.
items.howToFix: Remove looping pulse, glow, and hover-grow. On hover, change the color or the surface. If something enters, use one short fade.

items.title: Language of the page
items.why: Screen readers pronounce the page with the lang attribute. A missing lang is announced as the wrong language.
items.howToVerify: Find the html element. Pass if lang is set to the language the page is actually written in.
items.howToFix: Set the html lang attribute to the language of the page, such as en.

items.title: Keyboard access
items.why: Every control that a pointer can use needs a keyboard path.
items.howToVerify: Check menus, dialogs, and custom controls. Pass if they are real buttons or links, or have a key handler and a sensible role. A clickable div with no keyboard support does not pass.
items.howToFix: Use real buttons and links. Anything you can click should also work from the keyboard.

items.title: Skip link
items.why: A skip link lets keyboard users jump past a repeated header to the main content.
items.howToVerify: Look for a skip link that targets the main content and becomes available at the start of the tab order. Pass if it works. On a tiny single-screen page with no repeated nav, mark not applicable and say so.
items.howToFix: Add a Skip to content link as the first item in the tab order.

items.title: Color is not the only signal
items.why: Errors, success, and status that are only a color disappear for some people.
items.howToVerify: Review errors, badges, and charts. Pass if status also uses text, an icon, or a pattern. A red border alone does not pass.
items.howToFix: Add words or an icon next to any status that is currently only a color.

items.title: Links say where they go
items.why: "Click here" and "Read more" repeated ten times are useless out of context.
items.howToVerify: Read link text across the main pages. Pass if the text names the destination or action. Identical "Learn more" links with no surrounding context do not pass.
items.howToFix: Rename Click here and repeated Learn more links so each one says where it goes.

items.title: Compressed images
items.why: Uncompressed screenshots and camera files dominate the page weight of a vibe-coded app.
items.howToVerify: Inspect image files and image URLs. Pass if large images are compressed and use a sensible format such as WebP, AVIF, or an optimized JPEG or PNG. Multi-megabyte source exports do not pass. If the app has no content images, mark not applicable and say so.
items.howToFix: Replace large originals with compressed WebP, AVIF, or an optimized JPEG or PNG.

items.title: Images reserve their space
items.why: Width and height, or a reserved aspect ratio, keep the page from jumping when images arrive.
items.howToVerify: Check content images for width and height attributes or CSS that reserves the box. Pass if layout shift from images is prevented. If there are no content images, mark not applicable and say so.
items.howToFix: Set width and height, or a fixed aspect ratio, on content images so the layout does not jump.

items.title: Below-the-fold images lazy load
items.why: Images a person has not reached yet should not compete with the first screen.
items.howToVerify: Check images below the first screen for loading=lazy or an equivalent. The hero image should not be lazy. If there are no below-the-fold images, mark not applicable and say so.
items.howToFix: Add loading=lazy to images below the first screen. Leave the hero image eager.

items.title: No secrets in the repo or client bundle
items.why: A service key in the client, in a source file, or in git history people can clone, is already public.
items.howToVerify: Search tracked files, git history, and the frontend bundle for private keys, database passwords, connection strings, service-role tokens, and secret API keys. Pass if none are present. A secret that remains only in an old commit does not pass. A publishable client key that is designed to be public is not a secret. Do not copy any secret you find into the report; name the file and the kind of secret only.
items.howToFix: Remove private keys, database passwords, and secret tokens from the repo, its history, and the client bundle. Rotate any secret that was committed.

items.title: Build logs do not print secrets
items.why: A build or deploy log that prints the environment publishes every key to anyone who can open that log.
items.howToVerify: Read the CI config, the deploy config, and the build scripts. Pass if they do not print environment variables, connection strings, or the contents of .env. Pass if the project has no build or deploy log. A step that echoes the environment does not pass. Do not copy a secret from a log into the report.
items.howToFix: Stop printing environment values in the build and deploy logs. Rotate any key that already appeared there.

items.title: .env is gitignored
items.why: Environment files are where local secrets land. If git can see them, they will be committed.
items.howToVerify: Read .gitignore and see whether .env files are ignored. Fail if a real .env is tracked. Pass if ignore rules cover .env, or if the project has no env file and no server secret at all.
items.howToFix: Add .env to .gitignore. If a real env file was committed, stop tracking it and rotate the values.

items.title: Production does not serve .git or .env
items.why: A live site that serves its .git folder or a .env file hands out history and keys.
items.howToVerify: Find what the host deploys, and whether a request for /.git/config or /.env is blocked. Pass if production serves the built output and the repository folder is not on the public site. If there is no deployment, mark it missing and say that no production host config was found. A static host that publishes the project folder does not pass.
items.howToFix: Deploy the built output. Block requests for /.git and /.env on the host. Rotate any key that was ever committed.

items.title: HTTPS in production
items.why: A shipped app on plain HTTP leaks sessions and looks unfinished.
items.howToVerify: Find the public URL. Pass if it is served over HTTPS. Localhost alone does not pass this check for a finished app. If there is no deployment, mark it missing and say that no production URL was found.
items.howToFix: Serve the public site on https and redirect plain http to it.

items.title: DNS records still point at live services
items.why: A record left behind after you delete a host or a project lets someone else claim that name.
items.howToVerify: Look for DNS config in the repo, or a list of the public hostnames this app uses. Pass if each name still points at a service you control. A record for a removed project does not pass. If DNS is not in the repo, mark it missing and name the DNS host's record list as the setting to review. Do not claim a dashboard was checked when it is not in the workspace.
items.howToFix: In the DNS host, delete any record that still points at a project, host, or service you removed.

items.title: Security headers
items.why: Headers such as Content-Security-Policy, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a frame policy close common browser abuses.
items.howToVerify: Check the deployed response headers, or the host config that sets them. Pass if a content security policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a Referrer-Policy, and a framing control are set. The framing control is X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors rule. Say if the app is not deployed yet.
items.howToFix: On the host, set Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a Referrer-Policy, and either X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors rule.

items.title: Scripts you did not write are pinned or self-hosted
items.why: A script loaded from someone else's domain can be changed under you and then run for every visitor.
items.howToVerify: List script tags and loaders that fetch JavaScript from another host. Pass if each one is served from this app, or it is pinned with an integrity hash. A payment or auth script loaded from that provider's own domain can pass. A script from a CDN you do not control, with no integrity hash, does not pass. Fonts are a separate check. If the app loads no third-party script, pass and say so.
items.howToFix: Host those scripts yourself, or pin them with an integrity hash. Remove a script whose domain you no longer trust. A payment or auth script can stay on that provider's domain.

items.title: Protected routes
items.why: Account data, settings, and admin tools must not render for a signed-out visitor.
items.howToVerify: Open a private route, including any admin path, while signed out. Pass if the page, route handler, or server action checks authorization itself and refuses before private data is shown. A page that is only hidden by an unlisted URL does not pass. A check that lives only in framework middleware does not pass. If this app is Next.js, the installed release is 12.3.5, 13.5.9, 14.2.25, 15.2.3, or later on that line. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts or private areas.
items.howToFix: Check authorization inside the route or server action, and keep signed-out visitors away from private pages. On Next.js, upgrade to a release that fixes the middleware bypass, and keep the check in the route as well.

items.title: Each person can only reach their own data
items.why: A signed-in person who changes an id in the URL or the request can read, edit, or delete someone else's data.
items.howToVerify: Find reads, updates, and deletes of stored records. Pass if each one checks that the signed-in person owns that record, or is allowed to act on it. A private page that only checks that someone is signed in does not pass. A check that only hides a button in the browser does not pass. If the browser talks to the database directly, row policies have to enforce that ownership. A guessable id still has to fail for someone else's record. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts or stores no per-person data.
items.howToFix: On every read, update, and delete, check that the record belongs to the signed-in person before you touch it. If the client queries the database, turn on row policies that do the same check.

items.title: Private pages stay out of search
items.why: Inbox, settings, and admin URLs should not be indexed.
items.howToVerify: Check robots rules or a noindex tag on private routes. Pass if those routes are excluded. Mark not applicable when nothing is private.
items.howToFix: Add noindex on private pages, or disallow those paths in robots.txt.

items.title: Session cookie flags
items.why: A session cookie should be HttpOnly and Secure, with SameSite set, so scripts and stray requests have a harder time carrying it.
items.howToVerify: Find where the session cookie is set. Pass if HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite are set for production. Mark not applicable if the app does not use a session cookie.
items.howToFix: Set the session cookie to HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite in production.

items.title: The session is not in local storage
items.why: A token in local storage can be read by any script on the page. An HttpOnly cookie cannot.
items.howToVerify: Find where the session or access token is kept. Pass if it is an HttpOnly cookie, kept only in memory, or the auth provider stores it that way. Fail if the access token is written to localStorage or sessionStorage. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: Keep the session in an HttpOnly cookie. Remove access tokens from localStorage and sessionStorage.

items.title: Sessions expire
items.why: A login that never ends means the next person on a shared computer is still signed in.
items.howToVerify: Find the session. Pass if it ends after a set period of inactivity or a set lifetime. A sign-out button alone does not pass. The auth provider's lifetime counts. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: End the session after a period of inactivity. A day is a reasonable starting point.

items.title: Login tokens use a strong secret and a checked signature
items.why: A short or well-known signing secret lets someone mint a token that claims to be any account.
items.howToVerify: Find where session tokens or JWTs are signed and checked. Pass if an auth provider issues and verifies them, or the app reads a long random secret from the environment and verifies the signature on every request. A secret in source, a short or well-known secret, or a token accepted without a signature check does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: Read a long random signing secret from the environment. Verify the signature on every request. Remove any secret that was written into the code, and rotate it.

items.title: Server-side validation on public forms
items.why: Browser checks are a convenience. The server still has to reject bad or hostile input.
items.howToVerify: Find the handler that receives each public form. Pass if it validates and rejects invalid input on the server. Client-only checks do not pass. Mark not applicable when there is no form.
items.howToFix: Check every public form on the server and reject bad input there.

items.title: API input is checked on the server
items.why: A route that trusts the body or the query string can be talked into work you did not mean to do.
items.howToVerify: Find routes that read a body or query string from the caller. Pass if the server checks the type and rejects invalid input. Client checks do not pass. Mark not applicable when there is no API.
items.howToFix: Validate every API body and query parameter on the server, and reject what you do not expect.

items.title: Visitor input is not glued into a query or command
items.why: Text from a visitor, pasted into SQL, a NoSQL query, or a shell command, lets them change what the server runs.
items.howToVerify: Find database queries and shell commands that include visitor input. Pass if SQL uses parameters or a query builder, and commands do not insert that text. For a document database, pass if operator keys from the visitor, such as a field starting with $, are stripped before the query runs. Passing the request body straight into a query does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no database and builds no command from visitor input.
items.howToFix: Pass visitor values as parameters. Strip operator keys from document queries. Do not concatenate visitor text into SQL or a shell command.

items.title: The server does not fetch a URL from the visitor
items.why: A feature that requests an address the visitor chose can be aimed at a private service, or at the cloud metadata address that hands out the server's credentials.
items.howToVerify: Find server-side fetches whose URL comes from a request, a form, or stored visitor input. Pass if no such fetch exists. If one must exist, pass only when it allows hosts you listed and refuses private, link-local, and metadata addresses. On AWS, the instance metadata setting requires IMDSv2. Mark not applicable when the server never requests a URL that came from a visitor. If the app is not on AWS, the IMDSv2 part does not apply and you should say so.
items.howToFix: Stop requesting addresses a visitor supplied. If a fetch has to stay, allow only hosts you listed and refuse private and metadata addresses. On AWS, set the instance metadata service to require IMDSv2.

items.title: Visitor input never becomes a file path
items.why: A filename or path taken from a visitor can step outside the folder you meant to open, and read the server's own files.
items.howToVerify: Find file reads, writes, and deletes whose path, name, or template includes visitor input. Pass if the server never builds a path that way, or it maps the request to an id it issued and rejects a path that leaves the folder. Mark not applicable when the server does not touch the filesystem with visitor input. Package and server updates are still the dependency checks.
items.howToFix: Keep visitor input out of file paths. If you must open a file the person named, map it to an id you issued and reject a path that leaves the folder. Keep the server and its packages patched.

items.title: The server chooses which fields are saved
items.why: Saving the whole request body lets a person set their own role, price, or admin flag.
items.howToVerify: Find writes that take visitor input. Pass if the code lists the fields it saves. Writing the raw body onto a row does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no database.
items.howToFix: Copy only the fields you meant to store. Ignore role, price, and ownership fields sent by the visitor.

items.title: The server looks up the price
items.why: An amount that comes from the browser can be changed before it reaches the charge.
items.howToVerify: Find the code that creates a charge or a checkout session. Pass if the server looks up the amount from a product id it trusts. An amount, total, or discount taken from the request body does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app does not take payment.
items.howToFix: Have the browser send a product id. Look up the price on the server, and create the charge there.

items.title: A retry cannot create a second charge
items.why: A second tap on a slow connection can create a second charge, or a second record.
items.howToVerify: Find the payment request. Pass if the client makes one id when the person starts the action, sends it as an Idempotency-Key on every retry, and the button stays disabled while the request runs. Routes that create a record use the same key. A retry that can charge twice does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app does not take payment.
items.howToFix: Create one id at the start, send it as the Idempotency-Key on every retry, and keep the button disabled until the request finishes.

items.title: A limit and its update happen together
items.why: Two requests at the same moment can each pass a check you make first and write second, and spend a one-time code, a balance, or a quota twice.
items.howToVerify: Find one-time codes, balances, inventory counts, and usage quotas. Pass if the check and the update are one atomic step in the database, such as a conditional update or a transaction that fails when the value was already spent. A read, a decision in the app, and a later write do not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no code, balance, inventory count, or quota a second request could spend twice.
items.howToFix: Make the check and the update one conditional write or transaction. Reject the second request when the code, balance, or quota is already spent.

items.title: Every input has a label
items.why: Placeholder text disappears while typing and is not a name for the field.
items.howToVerify: Review each input, select, and textarea. Pass if each has a visible label tied to it. Placeholder-only fields do not pass.
items.howToFix: Add a visible label for every field and connect it with for and id.

items.title: Inline errors
items.why: An error has to say which field failed and how to fix it.
items.howToVerify: Submit a form with a bad value. Pass if the message sits with the field and is text, not color alone.
items.howToFix: Show the error in words next to the field, and say how to correct it.

items.title: Pending submit state
items.why: A slow submit without a pending state gets clicked again.
items.howToVerify: Submit a form. Pass if the button shows a pending state and cannot send a duplicate while the request is in flight.
items.howToFix: Disable the submit button and show a pending label while the request runs.

items.title: Success confirmation
items.why: Silence after submit looks like a failure.
items.howToVerify: Complete a valid submit. Pass if the form confirms success in text on the page or by moving to a confirmation screen. A cleared form with no message does not pass.
items.howToFix: After a valid submit, show a success message or move to the confirmation page.

items.title: Account settings
items.why: People who can sign in need a place to see and change the account.
items.howToVerify: Find the settings view for a signed-in person. Pass if they can review the account details the app stores. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: Add a settings page where a signed-in person can see and change the account.

items.title: A signed-in person can sign out
items.why: Sign-up, sign-in, and a reset path still leave someone stuck in the account on a shared computer if they cannot sign out.
items.howToVerify: Find a sign-out control. Pass if it ends the session. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: Add a sign-out control that ends the session.

items.title: Signup confirms the person is old enough
items.why: An account that collects an email from a child under 13, with no parent involved, is a COPPA problem.
items.howToVerify: Find the signup flow. Pass if it asks the person to confirm they are 13 or older, or it collects a birthdate and refuses younger signups. A product aimed at children passes only if a parent consents before any personal data is collected. Mark not applicable when the app has no signup.
items.howToFix: Add an age confirmation to signup. If the product is for children, collect the parent's consent before you ask the child for anything.

items.title: Email is verified before the account is active
items.why: A signup that trusts a typed email can lock a real person out, or open an account they never asked for.
items.howToVerify: Find signup. Pass if the person proves they control the email, with a link or code, before the account can be used. A magic link, a provider sign-in, or an auth setting that confirms email first also passes. A later sign-in with Google or another provider attaches only to an account that already proved it owns that email. Joining a provider sign-in to an unconfirmed account does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts, or the account has no email.
items.howToFix: Send a verification link or code and wait for it before the account is active. A magic link or provider sign-in can be the proof. Attach a provider sign-in only to an account that already owns that email.

items.title: Password reset or equivalent
items.why: Password accounts need a recovery path. Passwordless accounts need a way back in if the email or device changes.
items.howToVerify: Find the reset, magic-link, or recovery flow. Pass if a locked-out person has a real way back. A reset link or code expires and stops working after it is used. The link is built from a site URL in config. A link that changes when the request Host header changes does not pass. A provider-owned magic link passes when that provider expires it and builds it from the provider's site URL. Mark not applicable when there are no accounts.
items.howToFix: Add a reset link, magic link, or another real way back in. Build that link from the site URL in config. Make a reset link or code expire, and accept it only once.

items.title: People can delete their personal data
items.why: If the app stores personal data, people need a way to delete it. Keeping it with no way out is a problem in a lot of places, including Europe, even when you are based somewhere else.
items.howToVerify: Look in settings or the privacy policy for deletion. Pass if a person can actually delete the personal data you store. A way to export it as well belongs in a full pass. Export alone does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app stores no personal data.
items.howToFix: Add a way to delete the personal data you store, mention it in the privacy policy, and offer an export if you can.

items.title: Forms ask only for data the app uses
items.why: A phone number, birthday, or address the product never uses is data you cannot justify keeping.
items.howToVerify: Read signup and other forms. Pass if each required field is one the product actually uses. Mark not applicable when there is no form.
items.howToFix: Remove required fields the app does not use.

items.title: A plan for telling people about a breach
items.why: If account data leaks, you are expected to tell the people affected. A plan written after the breach is late.
items.howToVerify: Pass if the project has a short note of how you would tell affected people, and a way you would notice, such as an error monitor or the sign-in and error log. Mark not applicable when the app stores no personal data.
items.howToFix: Write down who you contact and how if account data leaks. Use an error monitor, or the log you already keep, so you notice.

items.title: Autocomplete on auth fields
items.why: Password managers need autocomplete hints such as username, current-password, and new-password.
items.howToVerify: Inspect the sign-in and sign-up fields. Pass if autocomplete is set to the right token. Mark not applicable when the app has no auth fields.
items.howToFix: Set autocomplete on sign-in fields to username, current-password, or new-password.

items.title: README explains how to run the app
items.why: A vibe-coded repo that only runs inside one chat session is not finished.
items.howToVerify: Read the README. Pass if a newcomer can install, configure, and run the app from what it says. A title with no steps does not pass.
items.howToFix: Write the install, setup, and run commands in the README.

items.title: A map of where things live
items.why: The next session should not have to open every file to learn where a feature lives.
items.howToVerify: Read the README or another short doc in the repo. Pass if it names the main parts of the project and where a feature lives. Pass if the project is a single file. A README that only lists install commands does not pass this check.
items.howToFix: Add a short map of the main folders or modules, and what each one is for.

items.title: A test covers a behavior that matters
items.why: A path nobody has run since the last change is how an app breaks after it ships.
items.howToVerify: Find the project's test command and at least one test of a behavior the product would break without, such as a permission check, a price, a form handler, or a calculation. Pass if that test is real and the command runs it. A test file that is never run does not pass. Pass if the project is static pages with no behavior to test.
items.howToFix: Add one automated test for a behavior that matters, and write the command that runs it.

items.title: .env.example without secrets
items.why: People need the variable names. They should never receive a real secret in the example file.
items.howToVerify: If the app needs environment variables, find .env.example or the documented list. Pass if names are listed and values are blank or fake. Fail if a real secret is in the example. Mark not applicable when the app needs no environment variables.
items.howToFix: Add .env.example with the variable names and blank or fake values. Remove any real secret.

items.title: No known high-severity holes in dependencies
items.why: A vibe-coded app often installs packages and never checks them. A published hole in a dependency is already public.
items.howToVerify: Look for a lockfile and an audit setup such as npm audit, pnpm audit, pip-audit, or Dependabot. Pass if no high or critical advisory is still open. Mark not applicable when the app installs no packages. Name the package and the severity only.
items.howToFix: Run the project's audit command. Update or replace each package with a high or critical advisory, then commit the lockfile.

items.title: Lockfile committed
items.why: Without a lockfile, the next install can pull different versions than the ones you shipped.
items.howToVerify: Find a committed lockfile such as package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, poetry.lock, or Cargo.lock. Mark not applicable when there are no dependencies.
items.howToFix: Generate the lockfile with the project's install command and commit it. Do not commit installed package folders.

items.title: Supported framework and runtime
items.why: Unsupported frameworks and runtimes stop receiving security fixes.
items.howToVerify: Compare the framework and runtime versions in the manifest, engines field, Dockerfile, or README with a release that still receives fixes. Pass if they are on a supported line. Mark not applicable when the app installs nothing and names no runtime.
items.howToFix: Upgrade the framework and runtime to a supported version, follow that project's upgrade notes, and reinstall from the lockfile.

items.title: A package earns its place
items.why: A package that only wraps the standard library is more code to trust, update, and ship.
items.howToVerify: Read the dependency manifest. Pass if each package does work the language or framework does not already do. A thin wrapper around a built-in does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app installs no packages.
items.howToFix: Remove a package that only wraps the standard library or the framework, and call the built-in instead.

items.title: Database backups
items.why: A database with no backup can lose people's data from one bad command.
items.howToVerify: Find a backup schedule, a host backup setting, or a documented restore step. A restore you have tried is part of a full pass. A backup with no written restore does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no database.
items.howToFix: Turn on automatic backups at the host, or schedule a dump, write down how to restore one, and try that restore on a copy.

items.title: Visitor text is escaped
items.why: Text a visitor typed, dropped straight into the page as HTML, lets them run script in someone else's browser.
items.howToVerify: Find where visitor text is shown. Pass if the framework renders it as text or it is escaped. Fail on raw HTML insertion of that text. Mark not applicable when the app never shows text a visitor submitted.
items.howToFix: Render that text as text. Remove raw HTML insertion, or sanitize with a maintained library only if rich text is required.

items.title: Passwords are hashed
items.why: A database of readable passwords is a breach the moment it leaks.
items.howToVerify: Find where passwords are saved. Pass if a password hashing function is used. Fail if passwords are stored or logged in plain text. Mark not applicable when the app never handles passwords.
items.howToFix: Hash passwords with the platform's password hasher before saving them. Stop logging password fields. If readable passwords were stored, make people set new ones.

items.title: Passwords have a minimum length
items.why: A very short password is easy to guess. Requiring a symbol does not fix a password that can be one character long.
items.howToVerify: Find where a password is chosen. Pass if new passwords must be at least 8 characters, or the auth provider enforces its own minimum length. A symbol rule with no minimum length does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app never handles passwords.
items.howToFix: Require at least 8 characters on new passwords, or turn on the auth provider's length rule.

items.title: Production hides internal errors
items.why: A stack trace, SQL error, or debug screen tells a stranger your paths, versions, and queries.
items.howToVerify: Find the production error response and any debug route. Pass if visitors see a generic message. A stack trace, a SQL error, a framework debug page, a database admin screen, a GraphQL playground, or a debug toolbar left on in production does not pass.
items.howToFix: Turn off debug mode in production, remove debug routes, and show the friendly error page instead.

items.title: Production source maps stay unpublished
items.why: A source map shipped with the live build lets someone rebuild the original code.
items.howToVerify: Check the production build settings and the files a publish would include. Pass if production source maps are off, or they are not deployed and not inside a published package. A setting that emits source maps for the production browser build does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app ships no JavaScript build and publishes no package.
items.howToFix: Turn off source maps for the production build. Before you publish a package, confirm the archive contains no source map of your original code.

items.title: The database is not open to the internet
items.why: A database that accepts connections from any address can be guessed at by the whole internet.
items.howToVerify: Find the database host settings. Pass if only the app can connect, the database requires a password, and the host limits which addresses are allowed. A port open to every address, or a database with no password, does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no database.
items.howToFix: Turn on the host's network allow-list or private networking, and require a password, so only the app can reach the database.

items.title: The database and file store are not wide open
items.why: Rules left open, or a public file bucket, let anyone read what you stored.
items.howToVerify: Find client-side database or storage rules, such as Firebase, Supabase, or S3. Pass if the client cannot read or write unless a rule allows that person, or only the server talks to the store and its key is not in the browser. A public bucket of private files, or a rule that allows every read and write, does not pass. Files that are meant to be public pass when the rule is limited to those files. Per-person ownership is a separate check. Mark not applicable when the app has no database and no hosted file store.
items.howToFix: Keep storage private. Scope each rule to the owner, or serve private files with a signed URL, before you deploy. Leave the service key on the server.

items.title: Sign-in failures and server errors are logged
items.why: Without a log, a burst of failed sign-ins or bad requests is invisible until something breaks.
items.howToVerify: Pass if failed sign-in attempts and server errors are written where the operator can read them. Passwords and session tokens are not in that log. If the app has an API, its errors are included. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: Log failed sign-ins and server errors. Leave passwords and session tokens out of the log.

items.title: Public forms are rate-limited
items.why: A public form with no limit is easy to hammer with a script.
items.howToVerify: Find the handler for a public form. Pass if repeated attempts are limited. Mark not applicable when there is no public form. Sign-in limits are a separate check.
items.howToFix: Limit how often those endpoints can be called, and show a try-again message when the limit is hit.

items.title: Failed sign-ins get slowed or blocked
items.why: Unlimited password guesses are how accounts get broken into.
items.howToVerify: Find the sign-in handler. Pass if a run of failed attempts is delayed or blocked for a while, both for that account and for that client or IP. The auth provider's own limit counts when it covers both. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: After repeated failed sign-ins, block or delay further tries for that account and for that IP, and tell the person to try again later.

items.title: Login, signup, and reset hide which emails exist
items.why: A different message for a real email than for a fake one lets someone test a list and learn who has an account.
items.howToVerify: Read the responses for login, signup, and password reset. Pass if each one says the same thing whether or not that email has an account, in the page and in the HTTP response. A message such as no account for that email, or email already registered, does not pass. A magic-link sign-in that always says to check email passes. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts.
items.howToFix: Use one generic message for login, signup, and reset, whether or not that email has an account. Do the same in the HTTP response.

items.title: Sign-in resists passwords leaked elsewhere
items.why: Bots try email and password pairs from other sites' breaches against this login.
items.howToVerify: Find password sign-in and password choice. Pass if new or attempted passwords are checked against known breaches, or the account can turn on a second factor. Both belong in a full pass. The auth provider's own breached-password check counts. Mark not applicable when the app has no accounts, or it never handles passwords.
items.howToFix: Turn on the auth provider's breached-password check, or reject passwords known from public breaches. Offer a second factor on the account.

items.title: Each person has a request ceiling
items.why: A route a script can call with no per-person limit is how a host decides the app is abuse and suspends it.
items.howToVerify: Find route handlers and server actions a person or a script can call repeatedly. Pass if each has a per-person or per-minute cap, or the host already enforces one. Sign-in limits and public-form limits count for those routes. Mark not applicable when there is no API or server action.
items.howToFix: Cap how often each person can call those routes, and return a try-again response when the cap is hit.

items.title: API origins are limited
items.why: An API that trusts every website can let another site act as a signed-in person.
items.howToVerify: Find the allowed-origins setting. Pass if credentialed calls are limited to your own sites. Mark not applicable when there is no API. A public API that does not use cookies can pass if that is stated.
items.howToFix: Allow only your real site origins. Do not use a wildcard origin together with credentials.

items.title: Uploads are limited
items.why: An upload with no type or size limit is how untrusted files land on the server.
items.howToVerify: Find the upload handler. Pass if it caps size and allows only expected types. Mark not applicable when nobody can upload a file.
items.howToFix: Reject oversized files and types you do not expect. Keep uploads that should not run out of the public web folder.

items.title: Email, text messages, paid APIs, and uploads have a ceiling
items.why: Hosts suspend apps that send unlimited email or text messages, call a paid API with no cap, or accept unlimited uploads. You pay for every text a script can trigger.
items.howToVerify: Find email sending, SMS sending, paid API calls, and uploads. Pass if each one that exists has a per-user or per-day cap, or the provider already enforces a quota. Text messages also stay inside the countries this product serves. Mark not applicable when the app sends no email, sends no SMS, calls no paid API, and nobody can upload a file.
items.howToFix: Cap emails and text messages per day, paid API calls per user, and uploads per account. Limit text messages to the countries you serve. A quota from the provider counts.

items.title: An AI feature has the least access it needs
items.why: Text a person types, or text on a page the model reads, can change what that feature does, including leaking its instructions or calling a tool it should not have.
items.howToVerify: Find features that send visitor text or page content to a model, and any tool the model can call. Pass if the tools are only what that feature needs, the instructions contain no secret, and an action that cannot be undone waits for a person to confirm it. A model that can read secrets, run arbitrary queries, or delete data on its own does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app has no such feature.
items.howToFix: Give the model only the tools that feature needs. Keep secrets out of its instructions. Ask a person to confirm any action that cannot be undone.

items.title: A model limit does not hang the page
items.why: When the model provider hits a limit or goes down, a spinner that never ends looks like the app froze.
items.howToVerify: Find the call to a model provider. Pass if a rate limit, a quota error, or an outage shows a clear message and a next step. A second provider you already configured is part of a full pass. A request that hangs with no message does not pass. Mark not applicable when the app does not call a model.
items.howToFix: Catch a rate limit or an outage from the model provider and show a clear message. Send the request to another provider you already trust if you have one.

items.title: Cookie actions check the sender
items.why: A cookie session that accepts a request from any site can be triggered by another page.
items.howToVerify: Find requests that change data and rely on the session cookie. Pass if they check a CSRF token or the origin. Mark not applicable when there is no cookie session.
items.howToFix: Require a CSRF token or a same-origin check on those requests.

items.title: Redirects stay on your site
items.why: A redirect that trusts a URL from the query string can send people to a lookalike site.
items.howToVerify: Search for redirects built from a query parameter, a form field, or a return URL after login. Pass if those targets stay on your own paths, or if no such redirect exists. A destination on another host does not pass unless it is on an allowlist written in the code.
items.howToFix: Redirect only to relative paths you control, or to a host on an allowlist. Ignore a full URL supplied by the visitor.

items.title: Payment webhooks check the signature
items.why: A webhook that trusts the body can be told a payment succeeded when nobody paid.
items.howToVerify: Find the route that receives payment events. Pass if it verifies the processor's signature and rejects a request without one. Mark not applicable when the app does not take payment, or it never receives webhooks.
items.howToFix: Verify the webhook signature with the processor's signing secret before you fulfill an order. Reject anything that does not match.

items.title: Refund or cancellation policy
items.why: Charging people with no written refund or cancellation rule is how a small app ends up in a dispute. A subscription has to say when it renews and how to cancel, next to the button that starts it.
items.howToVerify: Find a refund, cancellation, or billing policy linked from checkout or the terms. Pass if it says what happens after someone pays. If the charge renews, the subscribe button also shows the renewal price or period and how to cancel. Mark not applicable when the app does not take payment.
items.howToFix: Write a short refund or cancellation policy for this product and link it from checkout and the footer. Next to a subscribe button, state when it renews and how to cancel.

items.title: The payment processor allows this business
items.why: Stripe and PayPal freeze the account and hold the money when a product sits on their restricted list.
items.howToVerify: Read what the app sells and which processor it uses. Pass if it is an ordinary product, or the project shows that processor already approved a restricted category. Fail if it takes live card payments for adult content, gambling, weapons, drugs, crypto, file-sharing lockers, or money transmission with no sign of approval. Mark not applicable when the app does not take payment.
items.howToFix: Read the restricted-business list for the processor you use before you take a live payment. If the product is on that list, get their approval first or leave live charges off.

items.title: Marketing email is opt-in
items.why: Marketing email without consent, with no way to stop, or with no postal address, is a legal problem in many places.
items.howToVerify: Find newsletter or other marketing mail. Pass if people opt in, each marketing message has a working unsubscribe link, and the message shows a physical postal address. Mark not applicable when the app sends no marketing email. A receipt or password reset does not by itself make this apply.
items.howToFix: Make the marketing list opt-in. Put a working unsubscribe link and your physical postal address in those emails.

items.title: Images, fonts, and code are licensed
items.why: Shipping someone else's photo, font, icon set, or code without a license is a copyright problem.
items.howToVerify: Check images, fonts, and copied code for a license or a source you control. Pass if they are original or the license allows this use. Fail if a stock file, logo, or template is present with no license.
items.howToFix: Replace unlicensed files with ones you made or ones the license allows. Note the license in the repo.

items.title: Fonts load from your own site
items.why: A font file loaded from Google or another company sends the visitor's address to that company.
items.howToVerify: Pass if the app uses system fonts or serves font files from its own host. Fail if a page loads fonts from fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, or another font host you do not control.
items.howToFix: Serve the font files from your own site, or use a system font. Remove the Google Fonts link.

items.title: A way to report and remove user content
items.why: If visitors can post or upload, a host or a copyright owner will contact you. One illegal or copyrighted file with nobody to reach is how the app gets suspended. Hosting that content for people in the United States also needs a DMCA designated agent on file with the Copyright Office.
items.howToVerify: Pass if a public page or footer gives an email or form for content and copyright complaints, the app has a way to remove that post or file, and the terms or that page say what people are not allowed to post. If the product is offered to people in the United States, the page names a designated agent and points to the Copyright Office registration. Mark not applicable when visitors cannot publish text, images, or files that the app stores or shows. A contact form, login, or checkout does not count. A file the app keeps does count.
items.howToFix: Add a short page with an email for content and copyright complaints, say what content is not allowed, link it in the footer, and make sure you can delete what was posted or uploaded. If you offer this to people in the United States, name a designated agent and register that agent with the Copyright Office.

items.title: Reviews and stats are real
items.why: Invented reviews, user counts, or awards are a deception problem.
items.howToVerify: Look for testimonials, star ratings, and statistics. Pass if they come from real use or are clearly labeled as examples. Mark not applicable when the app shows none of these.
items.howToFix: Remove invented reviews and numbers, or replace them with ones you can stand behind.

items.title: Text responses are compressed
items.why: Uncompressed HTML, CSS, and JavaScript make the first visit slower than it looks.
items.howToVerify: Check the production host for gzip or brotli on text responses. Pass if compression is on. If the app is not deployed, mark it missing and say that no host config was found.
items.howToFix: Turn on gzip or brotli for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on the host.

items.title: The first page is not a huge script
items.why: A vibe-coded app often sends every library on the first page.
items.howToVerify: Look at the scripts on the first page or the main bundle. Pass if unused libraries are not in that first load. A mostly static page with little script passes.
items.howToFix: Remove libraries the first page does not use, and load the rest only on the screens that need them.

items.title: Text stays visible while fonts load
items.why: A custom font that blocks rendering leaves the page blank on a slow connection.
items.howToVerify: Pass if the app uses system fonts, or custom fonts set font-display to swap or optional so fallback text stays visible.
items.howToFix: Add font-display: swap to each custom font, or use a system font for interface text.
